quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Limit how far you ride in one day.

questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue when riding, dress for the weather. Ride no more than six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants. You may crash when they wear off.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and ride slowly toward it. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You rarely hear a tire going flat. You will usually notice it by how the motorcycle handles instead.

questions.question: Other drivers have trouble seeing motorcycles at night. What should you do?

options.text: Use your horn repeatedly at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle's headlights at night.

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down. Keep more distance between you and other vehicles. Use the headlights of cars ahead to help you see. Use your high beam unless another vehicle is near. Be ready to change your lane position.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT tell them to do?

options.text: Get on after you start the engine.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to stay quiet and still. This helps you focus on riding. Passengers should board only after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's stopping distance?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars stop in nearly the same distance. However, slippery pavement makes stopping very difficult for motorcycles.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which of the following is NOT important?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It must fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When turning through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Always stay on the left side of the lane.
Always stay on the right side of the lane.
Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Conditions can change at any time. Be ready to change your lane position. The best path through a curve may not follow the road's curve.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before slowing down to warn them.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before slowing down to warn them.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, flash your brake light before slowing down. The tailgater may not see hazards ahead that require traffic to slow down.

questions.question: What do motorcycle windshields do?

options.text: They work as well as a face shield.
They work as well as goggles.
They do not protect your eyes from the wind.
They protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: If road conditions make it harder to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Get closer to the vehicle ahead of you.
Stay farther back from the vehicle ahead of you.
Have someone else ride the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the vehicle ahead of you.
questions.explanation: You need more space to stop if road conditions are bad. Keep at least a three-second distance behind other vehicles. This is especially important on slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, at what blood alcohol level is a person age 21 or older legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol level of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When should a passenger get on a motorcycle?

options.text: As far back on the seat as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should get on after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as close to the driver as possible without blocking control. They should hold onto the driver's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Where should a motorcycle rider position themselves in their lane?

options.text: In different spots based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: In different spots based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on the road and traffic conditions around you.

questions.question: How do you stop a motorcycle quickly?

options.text: Use the rear brake hard, then slowly increase the front brake.

questions.explanation: Apply both brakes at the same time for a quick stop.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.explanation: Before carrying a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the correct settings for that weight.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: What should you do about the oily strip in the center of the lane?

options.text: Avoid it when the road is wet.
Ride only on it because it gives better grip.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Do not worry about oil in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from vehicles builds up in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, there is usually enough grip to ride safely over it. When wet, avoid it. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them tightly or put them in saddlebags. Placing loads high on a sissy bar or frame raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and throws off the balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: What braking mistake do most riders make in crashes?

options.text: Not braking hard enough on the front tire and braking too hard on the rear tire.
Braking too hard on the front tire and not hard enough on the rear tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not braking hard enough on the front tire and braking too hard on the rear tire.
questions.explanation: Studies show most riders involved in crashes do not brake hard enough on the front tire and brake too hard on the rear tire.

questions.question: How should you ride a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may mean moving from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. Is this safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Usually safe unless the road is wet.
Usually safe unless it is sunny.
Always safe no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for motorcycles. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side of it and stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar when you accelerate?

options.text: It feels like it lags behind.
It feels like it accelerates faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it lags behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. Because of its weight and inertia, it will feel like it is lagging behind when you accelerate.
